The manual checklist is ready: [issue-167-manual-checklist.md](issue-167-manual-checklist.md), about 60 checkboxes that you can tick in VS Code. Like the test reference, it's untracked at the repo root.

**Setup (section 0):**

- Room server on `:3002` (`yarn start` in your `excalidraw-room` checkout); app on `:3001` (`yarn start` on the feature branch).
- Room storage goes to the Excalidraw OSS **dev** Firebase project set in `.env.development`.
- Use three _different_ browsers or profiles as Alex, Blair and Casey, so each gets its own collaborator id and local storage.
- Keep the console open: any red error counts as a failure.

**Sections 1–7** follow the acceptance criteria in order. Each check is a short "do this → expect that", and the issue's own scenario is in there (Casey on "UI flow" when Alex deletes it). To test conflicts, take one browser offline with DevTools → Network → Offline, make a change on each side, then come back online.

**Items marked ★ can only be checked by hand.** Don't skip these:

- how thumbnails, tab avatars, the "Only you see this." note and the toast look, in light and dark theme and at phone width;
- the real socket reconnecting, including a room-server restart;
- real Firebase storage when you reload alone;
- deletions with the real clock: the tests only check what Collab hands to Portal, because the test clock makes every deletion look a day old;
- an element mid-drag when its page is deleted, which depends on timing;
- images re-uploaded on room start, the room size limit now covering every page, and saving when the tab closes.

**Section 9** spot-checks the merged page features (#157–#165, #80–#84) outside a room, to catch regressions.

Two timing details worth knowing:

- Room saves are throttled to about 20 seconds, so wait around 25 seconds after your last change before closing every browser for the storage checks.
- View mode toggles with **Alt+R**.

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  describe("opening a room link (the app's own join path)", () => {
    /**
     * Loads the app with the room link in the URL, as a joining user does.
     * The room's scene then reaches the editor as its initial data.
     */
    const openRoomLink = async () => {
      const previousCollab = window.collab;
      unmountComponent();
      // a fresh load: the old app's Collab must not be reused
      appJotaiStore.set(collabAPIAtom, null);
      mocks.handlers.clear();
      window.history.replaceState(
        {},
        "",
        `${window.location.origin}/#room=${ROOM.roomId},${ROOM.roomKey}`,
      );
      const rendering = render(<ExcalidrawApp />);
      await waitFor(() => expect(window.collab).not.toBe(previousCollab), {
        timeout: 5000,
      });
      await waitFor(
        () => expect(mocks.handlers.has("first-in-room")).toBe(true),
        { timeout: 5000 },
      );
      return rendering;
    };

    const expectRoomPagesShown = async () => {
      await waitFor(() =>
        expect(getPageIds()).toEqual([ARCHITECTURE.id, DATABASE.id]),
      );
      expect(getPageInfos()).toEqual(ROOM_PAGE_INFOS);
      expect(getPageElementIds()).toEqual([["box"], ["table"]]);
      // the open page is a room page, so its elements aren't hidden by the
      // safety net (they were all hidden while this bug was there)
      expect(h.app.getActivePageId()).toBe(ARCHITECTURE.id);
      expect(h.state.openPageId).toBe(ARCHITECTURE.id);
      expect(
        h.elements.filter((el) => !el.isDeleted).map((el) => el.id),
      ).toEqual(["box"]);
    };

    it("with others online: you get every room page, not a blank one", async () => {
      const rendering = await openRoomLink();

      await deliverPageData(roomPageData([ARCHITECTURE, DATABASE]));
      await deliverInit(roomElements());
      await rendering;

      await expectRoomPagesShown();
    });

    it("alone: the stored room's pages load, not a blank one", async () => {
      mocks.storedPageData = roomPageData([ARCHITECTURE, DATABASE]);
      mocks.storedRoomElements = syncInvalidIndices(roomElements());
      const rendering = await openRoomLink();

      await triggerServerEvent("first-in-room");
      await rendering;

      await expectRoomPagesShown();
    });
  });
});

describe("default page names after deleting pages", () => {
  const pagesNamed = (...names: string[]) =>
    names.map((name, i) => createPage(`p${i + 1}`, name));

  const namesAfterDeleting = (pages: DrawingPage[], ...ids: string[]) =>
    deletePages(pages, ids, pages[pages.length - 1].id, () => "new-page").pages.map(
      (page) => page.name,
    );

  it("deleting page 1 makes page 2 'Page 1'", () => {
    expect(
      namesAfterDeleting(pagesNamed("Page 1", "Page 2", "Page 3"), "p1"),
    ).toEqual(["Page 1", "Page 2"]);
  });

  it("keeps the names users gave their pages", () => {
    expect(
      namesAfterDeleting(
        pagesNamed("Page 1", "Architecture", "Page 3", "Database"),
        "p1",
      ),
    ).toEqual(["Architecture", "Page 2", "Database"]);
  });

  it("renumbers any 'Page <number>', e.g. 'Page 10000' third becomes 'Page 2'", () => {
    expect(
      namesAfterDeleting(pagesNamed("Page 1", "Notes", "Page 10000"), "p1"),
    ).toEqual(["Notes", "Page 2"]);
  });

  it("matches default names case-insensitively, ignoring outer spaces", () => {
    expect(
      namesAfterDeleting(pagesNamed("Page 1", " page 7 ", "PAGE 9"), "p1"),
    ).toEqual(["Page 1", "Page 2"]);
  });

  it("leaves names that only look similar", () => {
    expect(
      namesAfterDeleting(
        pagesNamed("Page 1", "Page 2a", "Pages 3", "Page", "Page -4", "Page 1.5"),
        "p1",
      ),
    ).toEqual(["Page 2a", "Pages 3", "Page", "Page -4", "Page 1.5"]);
  });

  it("a page already at its number keeps the same page object", () => {
    const pages = pagesNamed("Page 1", "Page 2");
    expect(renumberDefaultPageNames(pages, "Page")[1]).toBe(pages[1]);
  });

  it("deleting every page still leaves one 'Page 1'", () => {
    expect(
      namesAfterDeleting(pagesNamed("Page 1", "Notes"), "p1", "p2"),
    ).toEqual(["Page 1"]);
  });

  it("hasDefaultPageName", () => {
    expect(hasDefaultPageName({ name: "Page 12" }, "Page")).toBe(true);
    expect(hasDefaultPageName({ name: "Page 12 copy" }, "Page")).toBe(false);
    // the base name is matched literally, not as a pattern
    expect(hasDefaultPageName({ name: "P.ge 1" }, "Pa.e")).toBe(false);

    ).toEqual(["Page 1", "Page 2"]);

});

      act(() => {

        ).toEqual([

        ]),
      );

    it("a peer's delete brings its renames; we don't renumber on our own", async () => {
      const { firstPageId, secondPageId } = await startRoomOnFirstOfTwoPages();
      const before = window.collab.getPageData()!;

      // the deleting peer: page 1 gone, page 2 renamed "Page 1"
      await deliverPageData(
        getLocalPageChanges(
          before,
          getSharedPageInfos(before)
            .filter((page) => page.id !== firstPageId)
            .map((page) => ({ ...page, name: "Page 1" })),
          Date.now() + 1000,
        ),
      );

      expect(h.app.getPages().map((page) => [page.id, page.name])).toEqual([
        [secondPageId, "Page 1"],
      ]);
      // and nothing to send back: the names came with the delete
      sync();
      expect(getSentPageData()).toEqual([]);
    });
  });
});

Both bugs are fixed and tested. The full suite has 175 of 176 files passing (3123 tests); the only failures are the 3 known Windows font snapshots. Typecheck, ESLint and Prettier are clean, and nothing is committed yet.

## Bug 1: sharing left one blank page

**Cause:**

- Opening a room link (joining, or reloading as the person who shared) hands the room's scene to the editor as its _initial data_.
- The editor loads initial data through the same path #165 uses for opening a file. That path didn't find any pages in it, so it replaced every page with one new page under a new random id.
- The room's elements are tagged with the room's page ids, so on that new page the safety net hid all of them. That's the blank slate.
- My tests had joined by calling Collab directly, which skips that step, so they never caught it.

**Fix** ([excalidraw-app/App.tsx](excalidraw-app/App.tsx)):

- When joining a room, the scene handed to the editor now includes the room's pages, which Collab has already set up. The editor keeps exactly those pages, with the same ids, so the room is the one the person who shared it created, as with the pre-pages Share button.
- The hash-change path leaves pages out, because it only updates the scene.

**Tests:** two new tests join the way a real user does, by loading the app with the room link: once with others online and once alone (from storage). With the fix removed, both fail with exactly the symptom you saw: one random page instead of the room's two.

## Bug 2: page names didn't follow deletes

**Fix** ([pages.ts](packages/excalidraw/pages.ts)):

- After a delete, every page still named "Page" + space + number is renamed to "Page" plus its new position. Your examples:
  - "Page 2" becomes "Page 1" once page 1 is deleted;
  - "Page 10000" third in the list becomes "Page 3".
- Names you chose yourself are never changed, including near-misses like "Page 2a", "Pages 3" or "Page 1.5".
- Matching ignores case and outer spaces, like #160's name check.
- In a room only the deleting client renumbers. The renames reach everyone with the delete, so clients never fight over names.

**Existing tests I updated (they encoded the old intent):** four in `pages.test.tsx`. Three of them said "pages keep their names (#160)" (two #158 deleting-mode tests and #158's "all but current"); the fourth is #162's "folder removed once its pages are deleted". Each now expects the renumbered names, and each still checks what it was really about.

**New tests:** nine unit and editor tests for the rule, plus two room tests (renames are sent; a peer's renames arrive with the delete). With the renumbering removed, 10 tests fail.

## Notes updated

- [issue-167-tests.md](issue-167-tests.md): a new "Bug fixes from manual testing" section, the 4 changed tests listed, and every collabPages line link shifted to match the file.
- [issue-167-manual-checklist.md](issue-167-manual-checklist.md): new checks for joining by pasting the link and reloading the room link, and for renumbering (including your "Page 10000" case).

**One question (an assumption I haven't made):** should default names also renumber when pages are **reordered**? In PowerPoint a slide's number always follows its position, so after dragging "Page 3" to the top it would become "Page 1", and the others shift down. Right now only deleting renumbers, as you described. Yes or no?

After that, reply "Approved" for the final phase: commits, the PR draft, and the AI-log reminder.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-26 01:08:31Z)**_

It isn't something #167 introduced, and it isn't a deliberate choice in #167. It's how upstream Excalidraw already behaves, and `master` before #167 does the same.

**Why it happens** (both in code that predates #167):

1. **Changing the link fires the app's hash-change handler** ([App.tsx:540](excalidraw-app/App.tsx#L540)). That handler only ends the session when the new link is **not** a room link. A link to a _different_ room counts as a room link, so the current session is never stopped.
2. **The handler then calls `startCollaboration` with the new room.** That function returns immediately when a socket is already open ([Collab.tsx:539](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L539)), so you stay connected to the old room while the address bar shows the new one.

The code comes from upstream Excalidraw (it was moved into `excalidraw-app` in upstream PR #6987).

**What #167 changes on this path:** nothing about which room you're in. The bug 1 fix now leaves `pages` out on this hash-change path, so a link change can't disturb your pages; you just stay where you were.

**Is it in scope?** Not as written. The spec puts "rooms and clients" in #166, and nothing in #167's criteria covers switching rooms. It is a real usability gap, though, and with pages it matters more: someone could think they're editing room B's pages while still syncing room A's.

**If you want it fixed,** the PowerPoint-style behaviour would be: opening a link to a different shared deck opens that deck. Concretely:

- when the link points to a different room, leave the current room first (same as "Stop session", keeping your current pages as a local drawing);
- then join the new room, whose pages replace yours (AC 1.2).

That's about three lines in the hash-change handler and a couple of tests. Because it changes upstream behaviour outside the spec, I'd rather you decide:

- **fix it here, in #167**;
- **file it as a separate issue** (it fits #166's "rooms and clients"); or
- **leave it** and note it as Tech Debt (Encountered) in the PR.

The reorder-renumbering question from my last message is also still open: should default "Page N" names renumber when pages are reordered, not just deleted?

_**Agent - sidechain (2026-11-26 01:11:52Z)**_

`high effort → 4 inline angles (bugs + conventions) → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1` if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument, review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **4 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a short `summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing, or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions, off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks, wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established. If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees: does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc" inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Conventions candidates use the same `file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state which CLAUDE.md rule is broken instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Give each finding that is left its `severity`, as Output defines it. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "the problem, where it happens and what sets it off. Fix: the change to make",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash",
    "severity": "one of: important, nit, pre_existing"
  }
]
```

Every object carries every key shown above. Its `severity` is one of:

- `important`: a bug that should be fixed before merging because this change adds it or makes it worse. If someone can hit it, a rare trigger does not lower the severity.
- `nit`: a minor issue, worth fixing but not blocking: a broken CLAUDE.md rule, or a bug that harms nobody, such as a misleading log line.
- `pre_existing`: a bug that exists in the codebase but that this change did not introduce. A bug in unchanged lines is `pre_existing` if the change only fails to fix it, and `important` if the change re-exposes it.

A severity only labels and orders a finding: never drop one for its severity. When the limit forces a cut, cut the lowest-ranked first. Most severe means `important`, then `pre_existing`, then `nit`.

Write each `summary` in two or three short sentences. Start with the problem as a user of the code would see it. Next say where it happens and what sets it off. End with "Fix:" and the change to make, or what to check if you are not sure.

Beyond Phase 2's dedup, if the same mistake is repeated in several places, report it once and name the other places in its `summary`. Different mistakes stay separate findings, even when one change would fix them all.

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If nothing survives, return `[]`. Do not call the ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's output contract is the JSON block above.

import { reconcileElements } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw";
import { getDefaultAppState } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/appState";
import { restoreElements } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/data/restore";
import {
  PAGE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH,
  PAGE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH,
  getNextDefaultPageName,
  groupElementsByPageTag,
  normalizePageName,
} from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/pages";
import {
  generateFractionalIndexBetween,
  getElementPageId,
  hashElementsVersion,
  isValidFractionalIndex,
} from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { RemoteExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/data/reconcile";
import type { SharedPageInfo } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/pages";
import type {
  ExcalidrawElement,
  FractionalIndex,
  OrderedExcalidrawElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";
import type { AppState } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/types";

/**
 * Multi-page live collaboration (#167): pure helpers for keeping every
 * page of a room in sync.
 */

/**
 * `restoreElements` for a room's elements (every page's), page by page:
 * restoring also repairs order keys, which repeat across pages, so restoring
 * them together would reorder them.
 *
 * @param existingElements context for each page (e.g. repairing bindings):
 * our elements with the same page tag
 */
export const restoreElementsByPage = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  existingElements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[] | null,
  opts?: Parameters<typeof restoreElements>[2],
) => {
  const existingByPage = groupElementsByPageTag(existingElements ?? []);
  return [...groupElementsByPageTag(elements)].flatMap(
    ([pageId, pageElements]) =>
      restoreElements(
        pageElements,
        existingElements ? existingByPage.get(pageId) ?? [] : null,
        opts,
      ),
  );
};

/**
 * Reconciles two copies of a room's elements (every page's), page by page.
 * Each page orders its elements on its own (fractional indices repeat across
 * pages), so reconciling them together would reorder them. An element's
 * copies always have the same page tag, since tags never change.
 */
export const reconcileElementsByPage = (
  localElements: readonly OrderedExcalidrawElement[],
  remoteElements: readonly RemoteExcalidrawElement[],
  appState: AppState,
): OrderedExcalidrawElement[] => {
  const localByPage = groupElementsByPageTag(localElements);
  const remoteByPage = groupElementsByPageTag(remoteElements);
  const pageIds = new Set([...localByPage.keys(), ...remoteByPage.keys()]);
  return [...pageIds].flatMap((pageId) =>
    reconcileElements(
      localByPage.get(pageId) ?? [],
      remoteByPage.get(pageId) ?? [],
      appState,
    ),
  );
};

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// page data: what the room shares about each page
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A shared page value with the time it last changed, by the clock of the
 * client that changed it. Each field has its own time, so changes to
 * different fields of a page never overwrite each other.
 */
export type PageField = Readonly<{ value: string; updated: number }>;

/**
 * The page fields everyone in a room shares. Everything else about a page
 * (scroll, zoom, grid, `showThumbnail`) is personal and never sent.
 * `position` is a fractional order key: pages are ordered by it, ties broken
 * by page id.
 */
export const SHARED_PAGE_FIELDS = [
  "name",
  "description",
  "viewBackgroundColor",
  "position",
] as const;
export type SharedPageField = typeof SHARED_PAGE_FIELDS[number];

export type SharedPage = Readonly<
  { id: string } & Record<SharedPageField, PageField>
>;

/** the PAGE_DATA message payload, also kept in the room's stored document */
export type SharedPageData = Readonly<{
  /** live pages, in page order */
  pages: readonly SharedPage[];
  /**
   * deleted page ids → when they were deleted. Kept so deletion wins: a
   * page deleted here never comes back, whatever arrives later.
   */
  deletedPageIds: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
}>;

export const EMPTY_PAGE_DATA: SharedPageData = {
  pages: [],
  deletedPageIds: {},
};

const compareStrings = (a: string, b: string) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);

/** page order: by position, ties broken by page id */
const comparePages = (a: SharedPage, b: SharedPage) =>
  compareStrings(a.position.value, b.position.value) ||
  compareStrings(a.id, b.id);

export const isPageDeleted = (
  data: Pick<SharedPageData, "deletedPageIds">,
  pageId: string,
) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(data.deletedPageIds, pageId);

/**
 * The later change wins. Two changes to the same field of the same page at
 * the same time can't be told apart by page id, so the larger value wins:
 * every client picks the same one, whatever order they arrive in.
 */
const pickNewerField = (a: PageField, b: PageField): PageField =>
  a.updated !== b.updated
    ? a.updated > b.updated
      ? a
      : b
    : a.value >= b.value
    ? a
    : b;

const mergePage = (a: SharedPage, b: SharedPage): SharedPage => ({
  id: a.id,
  name: pickNewerField(a.name, b.name),
  description: pickNewerField(a.description, b.description),
  viewBackgroundColor: pickNewerField(
    a.viewBackgroundColor,
    b.viewBackgroundColor,
  ),
  position: pickNewerField(a.position, b.position),
});

/**
 * Pages whose names collide (case-insensitive, trimmed) after changes crossed
 * in transit: the page whose name changed later is renamed to the next free
 * default name ("Page N"), ties broken by page id (the larger id is
 * renamed). The new name's time is one after the renamed change, so every
 * client computes the same field.
 */
export const resolvePageNameCollisions = (
  data: SharedPageData,
  baseName: string,
): SharedPageData => {
  const byNameTime = [...data.pages].sort(
    (a, b) => a.name.updated - b.name.updated || compareStrings(a.id, b.id),
  );
  const names = new Map(data.pages.map((page) => [page.id, page.name]));
  const taken = new Set<string>();
  const renamed = new Map<string, PageField>();
  for (const page of byNameTime) {
    const name = normalizePageName(page.name.value);
    if (!taken.has(name)) {
      taken.add(name);
      continue;
    }
    const value = getNextDefaultPageName(
      [...names.values()].map((field) => ({ name: field.value })),
      baseName,
    );
    const field = { value, updated: page.name.updated + 1 };
    names.set(page.id, field);
    renamed.set(page.id, field);
    taken.add(normalizePageName(value));
  }
  if (!renamed.size) {
    return data;
  }
  return {
    ...data,
    pages: data.pages.map((page) =>
      renamed.has(page.id) ? { ...page, name: renamed.get(page.id)! } : page,
    ),
  };
};

/**
 * When concurrent deletions leave no page at all, every client adds the same
 * blank page (same id, name and position), so they still agree.
 */
const getBlankPageAfterDeletions = (
  deletedPageIds: SharedPageData["deletedPageIds"],
  baseName: string,
): SharedPage => {
  const [id, updated] = Object.entries(deletedPageIds).sort(
    ([idA, a], [idB, b]) => b - a || compareStrings(idA, idB),
  )[0];
  const field = (value: string): PageField => ({ value, updated });
  return {
    id: `${id}-blank`,
    name: field(getNextDefaultPageName([], baseName)),
    description: field(""),
    viewBackgroundColor: field(getDefaultAppState().viewBackgroundColor),
    position: field(generateFractionalIndexBetween(null, null)),
  };
};

/**
 * Merges two copies of a room's page data (#167). The result is the same
 * whatever order changes arrive in:
 * - each field of each page: the later change wins (`pickNewerField`)
 * - deletion wins: a deleted page never comes back, even if edited later
 * - colliding names are resolved (`resolvePageNameCollisions`)
 *
 * @param baseName the default page name, e.g. "Page"
 */
export const mergePageData = (
  local: SharedPageData,
  remote: SharedPageData,
  baseName: string,
): SharedPageData => {
  const deletedPageIds: Record<string, number> = { ...local.deletedPageIds };
  for (const [id, deletedAt] of Object.entries(remote.deletedPageIds)) {
    deletedPageIds[id] = Math.max(deletedPageIds[id] ?? deletedAt, deletedAt);
  }

  const byId = new Map(local.pages.map((page) => [page.id, page]));
  for (const page of remote.pages) {
    const ours = byId.get(page.id);
    byId.set(page.id, ours ? mergePage(ours, page) : page);
  }
  let pages = [...byId.values()].filter(
    (page) => !isPageDeleted({ deletedPageIds }, page.id),
  );
  if (!pages.length && Object.keys(deletedPageIds).length) {
    pages = [getBlankPageAfterDeletions(deletedPageIds, baseName)];
  }

  return resolvePageNameCollisions(
    { pages: pages.sort(comparePages), deletedPageIds },
    baseName,
  );
};

/**
 * Indices (into `values`) of a longest strictly increasing subsequence. The
 * pages at these indices kept their relative order, so only the others moved.
 */
const getLongestIncreasingRun = (values: readonly number[]): Set<number> => {
  const lengths = values.map(() => 1);
  const previous = values.map(() => -1);
  for (let i = 0; i < values.length; i++) {
    for (let j = 0; j < i; j++) {
      if (values[j] < values[i] && lengths[j] + 1 > lengths[i]) {
        lengths[i] = lengths[j] + 1;
        previous[i] = j;
      }
    }
  }
  const kept = new Set<number>();
  let i = values.length ? lengths.indexOf(Math.max(...lengths)) : -1;
  while (i !== -1) {
    kept.add(i);
    i = previous[i];
  }
  return kept;
};

/**
 * Order keys for `pages` in their local order: pages that kept their
 * relative order keep their keys (null), the others (moved or new) get new
 * keys between their neighbours.
 */
const getPositions = (
  shared: SharedPageData,
  pages: readonly SharedPageInfo[],
): (string | null)[] => {
  const sharedIndex = new Map(shared.pages.map((page, i) => [page.id, i]));
  const known = pages
    .map((page, i) => ({ i, sharedIndex: sharedIndex.get(page.id) }))
    .filter(
      (entry): entry is { i: number; sharedIndex: number } =>
        entry.sharedIndex !== undefined,
    );
  const keptRun = getLongestIncreasingRun(
    known.map((entry) => entry.sharedIndex),
  );
  const keepsKey = new Set(
    known.filter((_, k) => keptRun.has(k)).map((entry) => entry.i),
  );
  const keyOf = (i: number) =>
    shared.pages[sharedIndex.get(pages[i].id)!].position.value;

  // new pages before every kept page go before every known page, e.g. the
  // blank page left by deleting every page becomes the first page
  const firstKnownKey = shared.pages[0]?.position.value ?? null;
  const positions: (string | null)[] = [];
  let lower: string | null = null;
  for (let i = 0; i < pages.length; i++) {
    if (keepsKey.has(i)) {
      positions.push(null);
      lower = keyOf(i);
      continue;
    }
    let next = i + 1;
    while (next < pages.length && !keepsKey.has(next)) {
      next++;
    }
    const upper =
      next < pages.length ? keyOf(next) : lower === null ? firstKnownKey : null;
    const key: string = generateFractionalIndexBetween(
      lower as FractionalIndex | null,
      upper as FractionalIndex | null,
    );
    positions.push(key);
    lower = key;
  }
  return positions;
};

/** fresh keys for every page, in order (fallback when keys can't fit) */
const getFreshPositions = (pages: readonly SharedPageInfo[]) => {
  let lower: string | null = null;
  return pages.map(() => {
    lower = generateFractionalIndexBetween(
      lower as FractionalIndex | null,
      null,
    );
    return lower;
  });
};

/**
 * Turns the editor's pages into page data, given the last shared copy (#167):
 * pages that are new, changed, moved or gone are recorded as changed `now`.
 * Returns null when nothing shared changed (personal settings never count).
 *
 * @param pages the editor's pages, in order
 */
export const getLocalPageChanges = (
  shared: SharedPageData,
  pages: readonly SharedPageInfo[],
  now: number,
): SharedPageData | null => {
  const sharedById = new Map(shared.pages.map((page) => [page.id, page]));
  const localIds = new Set(pages.map((page) => page.id));
  let changed = false;

  const deletedPageIds: Record<string, number> = { ...shared.deletedPageIds };
  for (const page of shared.pages) {
    if (!localIds.has(page.id)) {
      deletedPageIds[page.id] = now;
      changed = true;
    }
  }

  let positions: (string | null)[];
  try {
    positions = getPositions(shared, pages);
  } catch {
    // e.g. two pages with the same key around a moved page: renumber all
    positions = getFreshPositions(pages);
  }

  const toField = (
    previous: PageField | undefined,
    value: string,
  ): PageField => {
    if (previous && previous.value === value) {
      return previous;
    }
    changed = true;
    return { value, updated: now };
  };

  const sharedPages = pages.map((page, i): SharedPage => {
    const previous = sharedById.get(page.id);
    const position = positions[i];
    return {
      id: page.id,
      name: toField(previous?.name, page.name),
      description: toField(previous?.description, page.description),
      viewBackgroundColor: toField(
        previous?.viewBackgroundColor,
        page.viewBackgroundColor,
      ),
      position:
        position === null
          ? previous!.position
          : toField(previous?.position, position),
    };
  });

  return changed
    ? { pages: sharedPages.sort(comparePages), deletedPageIds }
    : null;
};

/**
 * A fingerprint of a room's elements (every page's, in page order), to tell
 * whether anything changed since the last broadcast. A sum of versions
 * (`getSceneVersion`) can come out the same when a deleted page's elements
 * go away and new ones are drawn; this hash of `versionNonce`s changes with
 * any edit, addition or removal.
 */
export const getRoomVersion = (elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[]) =>
  hashElementsVersion(elements);

/** drops elements tagged for a deleted page (delete wins, #167) */
export const excludeElementsOnDeletedPages = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  pageData: SharedPageData,
): T[] =>
  elements.filter((element) => {
    const pageId = getElementPageId(element);
    return !pageId || !isPageDeleted(pageData, pageId);
  });

/** the pages as the editor shows them, in order */
export const getSharedPageInfos = (data: SharedPageData): SharedPageInfo[] =>
  data.pages.map((page) => ({
    id: page.id,
    name: page.name.value,
    description: page.description.value,
    viewBackgroundColor: page.viewBackgroundColor.value,
  }));

const toComparable = (data: SharedPageData) =>
  JSON.stringify({
    pages: [...data.pages].sort(comparePages),
    deletedPageIds: Object.entries(data.deletedPageIds).sort(([a], [b]) =>
      compareStrings(a, b),
    ),
  });

export const isSamePageData = (a: SharedPageData, b: SharedPageData) =>
  toComparable(a) === toComparable(b);

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// validation of page data from peers and room storage
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

const isRecord = (value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> =>
  typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);

const isPageField = (value: unknown): value is PageField =>
  isRecord(value) &&
  typeof value.value === "string" &&
  typeof value.updated === "number" &&
  Number.isFinite(value.updated);

const parseSharedPage = (value: unknown): SharedPage | null => {
  if (
    !isRecord(value) ||
    typeof value.id !== "string" ||
    !value.id ||
    !SHARED_PAGE_FIELDS.every((field) => isPageField(value[field]))
  ) {
    return null;
  }
  const page = value as SharedPage;
  const name = page.name.value.trim();
  if (
    !name ||
    name.length > PAGE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH ||
    page.description.value.length > PAGE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH ||
    !isValidFractionalIndex(page.position.value, undefined, undefined)
  ) {
    return null;
  }
  // only the known fields: nothing else from a peer reaches the editor
  const pick = (field: PageField): PageField => ({
    value: field.value,
    updated: field.updated,
  });
  return {
    id: page.id,
    name: pick(page.name),
    description: pick(page.description),
    viewBackgroundColor: pick(page.viewBackgroundColor),
    position: pick(page.position),
  };
};

/**
 * Validates page data from a peer or the room's storage (#167). Returns null
 * (ignore all of it, keep the pages as they are) for a page with missing or
 * invalid fields, two pages with the same id, no live page, or an invalid
 * deleted-page entry.
 */
export const parsePageData = (value: unknown): SharedPageData | null => {
  if (
    !isRecord(value) ||
    !Array.isArray(value.pages) ||
    !value.pages.length ||
    !isRecord(value.deletedPageIds)
  ) {
    return null;
  }
  const pages: SharedPage[] = [];
  const ids = new Set<string>();
  for (const candidate of value.pages) {
    const page = parseSharedPage(candidate);
    if (!page || ids.has(page.id)) {
      return null;
    }
    ids.add(page.id);
    pages.push(page);
  }
  const deletedPageIds: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const [id, deletedAt] of Object.entries(value.deletedPageIds)) {
    if (!id || typeof deletedAt !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(deletedAt)) {
      return null;
    }
    deletedPageIds[id] = deletedAt;
  }
  return { pages: pages.sort(comparePages), deletedPageIds };
};
import { PAGE_ID_KEY, getElementPageId } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

/**
 * Page tags (#167), like the creator stamp (see creatorStamp.ts): every
 * element in a room carries the id of the page it was created on. The tag is
 * set once and never changed, so editing or moving the element, or
 * reordering or deleting other pages, never moves it to another page.
 */

/** elements without a page tag yet (new, or from before the tag existed) */
export const getElementsToPageStamp = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
): T[] => elements.filter((element) => getElementPageId(element) === null);

export const getPageStampedCustomData = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  pageId: string,
): NonNullable<ExcalidrawElement["customData"]> => ({
  ...element.customData,
  [PAGE_ID_KEY]: pageId,
});

import { CREATOR_ID_KEY } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

/**
 * Elements this client introduced to the room that don't carry its creator
 * stamp yet: newly drawn, pasted or duplicated (new id, possibly with a
 * copied foreign stamp), or restored by undo/redo without the stamp.
 *
 * Elements first received from other clients are never (re)stamped, so edits
 * never transfer ownership.
 *
 * @param remoteElementIds ids of elements that first reached this client from
 * the room (other clients or the room's stored scene)
 */
export const getElementsToStamp = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  remoteElementIds: ReadonlySet<string>,
  clientId: string,
): T[] =>
  elements.filter(
    (element) =>
      !element.isDeleted &&
      !remoteElementIds.has(element.id) &&
      element.customData?.[CREATOR_ID_KEY] !== clientId,
  );

export const getStampedCustomData = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  clientId: string,
): NonNullable<ExcalidrawElement["customData"]> => ({
  ...element.customData,
  [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: clientId,
});

  if (
    // bail if no room exists as there's nothing we can do at this point
    !roomId ||
    !roomKey ||
    !socket ||
    isSavedToFirebase(portal, elements, pageData)
  ) {
    return null;
  }

  const firestore = _getFirestore();
  const docRef = doc(firestore, "scenes", roomId);

  const storedScene = await runTransaction(firestore, async (transaction) => {
    const snapshot = await transaction.get(docRef);

    if (!snapshot.exists()) {
      const storedScene = await createFirebaseSceneDocument(
        elements,
        pageData,
        roomKey,
      );

      transaction.set(docRef, storedScene);

      return storedScene;
    }

    const prevStoredScene = snapshot.data() as FirebaseStoredScene;
    const prevStoredElements = getSyncableElements(
      // page by page (#167)
      restoreElementsByPage(
        await decryptElements(prevStoredScene, roomKey),
        null,
      ),
    );
    // don't save our live copies of elements whose deletion expired
    const expiredIds = isKnownToRoom
      ? new Set(
          getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion(
            elements,
            new Set(prevStoredElements.map((el) => el.id)),
            isKnownToRoom,
          ).map((el) => el.id),
        )
      : new Set<string>();
    const reconciledElements = getSyncableElements(
      reconcileElementsByPage(
        elements.filter((el) => !expiredIds.has(el.id)),
        prevStoredElements as OrderedExcalidrawElement[] as RemoteExcalidrawElement[],
        appState,
      ),
    );
    // the same merge as for peers' page data, so storage converges too
    const prevPageData = await decryptPageData(prevStoredScene, roomKey);
    const mergedPageData =
      pageData && prevPageData
        ? mergePageData(prevPageData, pageData, t("labels.page"))
        : pageData ?? prevPageData;

    const storedScene = await createFirebaseSceneDocument(
      // a deleted page's elements go with it, whoever still had them
      mergedPageData
        ? excludeElementsOnDeletedPages(reconciledElements, mergedPageData)
        : reconciledElements,
      mergedPageData,
      roomKey,
    );

    transaction.update(docRef, storedScene);

    // Return the stored elements as the in memory `reconciledElements` could have mutated in the meantime
    return storedScene;
  });

  const storedElements = getSyncableElements(
    restoreElementsByPage(await decryptElements(storedScene, roomKey), null),
  );
  const storedPageData = await decryptPageData(storedScene, roomKey);

  FirebaseSceneVersionCache.set(socket, storedElements, storedPageData);

  broadcastScene = async (
    updateType: WS_SUBTYPES.INIT | WS_SUBTYPES.UPDATE,
    elements: readonly OrderedExcalidrawElement[],
    syncAll: boolean,
  ) => {
    if (updateType === WS_SUBTYPES.INIT && !syncAll) {
      throw new Error("syncAll must be true when sending SCENE.INIT");
    }

    // sync out only the elements we think we need to to save bandwidth.
    // periodically we'll resync the whole thing to make sure no one diverges
    // due to a dropped message (server goes down etc).
    const syncableElements = elements.reduce((acc, element) => {
      if (
        (syncAll ||
          !this.broadcastedElementVersions.has(element.id) ||
          element.version > this.broadcastedElementVersions.get(element.id)!) &&
        isSyncableElement(element)
      ) {
        acc.push(element);
      }
      return acc;
    }, [] as SyncableExcalidrawElement[]);

    // nothing new to send (e.g. only a deleted page's elements went away, #167)
    if (!syncAll && !syncableElements.length) {
      return;
    }

    const data: SocketUpdateDataSource[typeof updateType] = {
      type: updateType,
      payload: {
        elements: syncableElements,
        ...(updateType === WS_SUBTYPES.UPDATE ? { sentAt: Date.now() } : {}),
      },
    };

    for (const syncableElement of syncableElements) {
      this.broadcastedElementVersions.set(
        syncableElement.id,
        syncableElement.version,
      );
    }

    this.queueFileUpload();

    await this._broadcastSocketData(data as SocketUpdateData);
  };

  private destroySocketClient = (opts?: { isUnload: boolean }) => {
    this.lastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion = -1;
    this.remoteElementIds = new Set();
    this.storedElementIds = new Set();
    // the room's pages stay as our local pages (#167); only the sync stops
    this.pageData = null;
    this.pendingElements = new Map();
    this.portal.close();
    this.fileManager.reset();
    if (!opts?.isUnload) {
      this.setIsCollaborating(false);
      this.setActiveRoomLink(null);
      this.collaborators = new Map();
      this.collaboratorDirectory = new Map();
      this.directoryRoomId = null;
      this.settingsRoomId = null;
      this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
        collaborators: this.collaborators,
        appState: {
          // back to solo: no directory (every creator its own bucket) and
          // nothing hidden
          collaboratorDirectory: null,
          hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(),
        },
      });
      LocalData.resumeSave("collaboration");
    }
  };

export const updateStaleImageStatuses = (params: {
  excalidrawAPI: ExcalidrawImperativeAPI;
  erroredFiles: Map<FileId, true>;
  elements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[];
}) => {
  if (!params.erroredFiles.size) {
    return;
  }
  params.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
    elements: params.excalidrawAPI
      .getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted()
      .map((element) => {
        if (
          isInitializedImageElement(element) &&
          params.erroredFiles.has(element.fileId)
        ) {
          return newElementWith(element, {
            status: "error",
          });
        }
        return element;
      }),
    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
  });

          secondPageId,

The full run a few minutes earlier, on the same product code, had none of them. The only change since then is cleanup in one test file, which none of those six import.

## Bug hunt: 8 real bugs found and fixed

An independent code review of the whole diff reported 10 findings. I checked each against the code: 8 were real, and I fixed them. Each has a test that I confirmed **fails with its fix removed**.

| # | Bug | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A **pasted or duplicated** element kept its source page's tag. It was hidden where you pasted it, and peers drew it on the source page. | Your own copies are re-tagged with the page they're on; elements from the room never are |
| 2 | **Images on pages that weren't open** never became "saved", so peers never loaded them | Upload status updates on every page |
| 3 | The "already saved" check compared raw JSON, so identical page data in a different order never matched, causing endless saves and an always-on "leave page?" prompt | Compare a canonical form |
| 4 | If a peer's elements arrived before their page data, a **joiner's blank page** was shared into the room for everyone | With peers online, a joiner waits for their page data |
| 5 | Renumbering after a delete got a fresh time, so it could **overwrite a collaborator's rename** made meanwhile | A renumber counts as just after the old name, so a real rename wins |
| 6 | Stored elements for a page not known yet were **dropped** | Held until the page arrives, like peers' elements |
| 7 | While **following**, any page you opened yourself was undone by their next mouse move | Follow only when _their_ page changes |
| 8 | After leaving and keeping the room, **images on other pages** weren't saved locally | Reset image status on every page |

**Two findings I didn't act on:**

- **A page created mid-join is lost.** The editor shows its loading screen during a join, so you can't create one then.
- **A page you named "Page 7" yourself gets renumbered.** That's the rule you asked for.

**I also found and fixed a test-isolation leak.** Collab throttles its room saves, so a save scheduled in one test could fire during the next. That made two tests flaky, only in slow (coverage) runs. Each test now cancels its pending saves when it ends, and three coverage runs in a row passed.

**One more test:** pasting a room link into a tab that's already open. This closes bug 1's last uncovered path, and it fails if `pages` leaks into the editor's state.

| Scope | Covered | % |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every added line | 1936 / 1990 | **97.3%** |
| Without `types.ts` (type declarations, no runtime code) | 1936 / 1965 | **98.5%** |

**At 100% of their lines:** `pageStamp.ts`, `pageSync.ts`, `pages.ts`, `Pages.tsx`, `Portal.tsx`, `LayerUI.tsx`, `excalidraw-app/App.tsx` (was 38%), and every other changed file except the three below. `pageSync.ts` also has 99.4% of its branches covered.

The few lines left in `Collab.tsx` (95.8%), editor `App.tsx` (98.8%), `PageInfoDialog.tsx` and `firebase.ts` (one line) are v8 mapping noise: comments, blank lines, or code that mutation checks prove runs.

**Other checks:** typecheck, ESLint and Prettier are clean. Both reference notes are updated: [issue-167-tests.md](issue-167-tests.md) has a new "Bugs found in the code review" section, and its line links are corrected after the inserted tests.

**I took "it all works" as a no on both open questions.** Default names renumber only on delete, not on reorder. Switching to a different room link while in a room keeps upstream Excalidraw's behaviour (you stay in the old room); I'll list it in the PR under Tech Debt (Encountered). Tell me if you meant either differently.

The architecture page is updated (same link): **[Multi-Page Collab Architecture](https://claude.ai/artifact/E4v8L9E8BeEGra6hmNNaWT)**. The flowcharts for the local edit, lifecycle, delete and follow paths now include the fixes, and a new section 12 lists every change made after the first version. Here's the recap.

## 1. The flow (what #167 does)

1. **Local edit.** You draw or change a page, and App's `onChange` calls `Collab.syncElements`. Collab then:
   - stamps new elements with `creatorId` and `pageId`;
   - compares your pages with the last shared copy and sends `PAGE_DATA` if anything shared changed;
   - announces your page if you switched;
   - sends the changed elements from every page;
   - queues a room save of every page plus the page data.
2. **A peer's elements arrive.**
   - Untagged elements are stamped with the first page.
   - Restore and reconcile run **per page**.
   - Each page's result goes to that page: the open page through the scene, other pages into storage, which redraws their previews.
   - Elements for a page we don't have yet are held; elements for a deleted page are dropped.
3. **Page data arrives.** It's validated (bad data is ignored as a whole), then merged:

   - later change wins, per field;
   - a deleted page never comes back;
   - a name clash becomes "Page N".

   Then `applySharedPages` updates the editor's pages.

4. **Starting a room:** every page goes in, stamped. **Joining:** your pages are replaced by the room's. **Reconnecting:** the client catches up from storage and sends its own changes. **Leaving:** the room's pages stay as your drawing.
5. **Presence.** Every presence message carries the sender's page. Other pages' cursors, selections and laser trails aren't drawn, tabs show avatars, and follow mode moves you to the person's page.
6. **Rules.**
   - Safety net: an element tagged for another page is treated like a hidden collaborator's.
   - View mode: you can switch pages and follow, but not change pages.
   - Hide and lock apply on every page and in previews.
   - Folders are off in a room.

## 2. Modifications to the original framework

- **Element package** (`ownership.ts`): the page tag, added to the existing #80 visibility rule.
- **Editor:**
  - App's adapter API: `getPages`, `setPageElements`, `applySharedPages`, `resetPages`, `selectPage`;
  - the local `openPageId`;
  - the renderer, canvas and laser-trail filters;
  - the page list (avatars, filtered previews), the info dialog note, and the Pages button in view mode;
  - clearing marks elements deleted;
  - deleting renumbers default names.
- **Host app:**
  - Collab and Portal sync every page and add the `PAGE_DATA` message;
  - Firebase stores page data;
  - two new pure modules, `pageStamp.ts` and `pageSync.ts`.
- **Unchanged:** the room server.

## 3. Changes to the flow since the first version

| Change | Flow affected |
| --- | --- |
| Joining via the room link keeps the room's pages (manual bug 1) | Join → the editor's initial load |
| Deleting renumbers "Page N" names to their position (manual bug 2) | Delete |
| Pasted copies re-tagged with the page they're on | Local edit (stamping) |
| Image statuses updated on every page | Upload, and leaving the room |
| A joiner with peers online waits for their page data | Join |
| A renumber counts as just after the old name | Page-data merge |
| Stored elements for unknown pages are held | Join from storage |
| Follow only when their page changes | Presence |
| "Already saved" compares a canonical form | Room save |

## 4. Changes to test cases

**Existing tests from other issues that I changed:**

- `collab.test` (#80): the room creator's elements also carry `pageId` (AC 2.1).
- `collabNewcomer` AC-H (#83): the mock returns page data, and the fixture is a real stored room with one page.
- `collabVisibility` (#80): a newcomer gets `PAGE_DATA` first.
- `history.test`: the snapshot helper drops the random `openPageId`.
- `pages.test` #159 "clear all": checks _live_ elements (cleared pages keep their deleted copies).
- `pages.test` #158 / #162: four tests now expect renumbered names, which was bug 2's intent change.

**My own tests that I corrected along the way:**

- A step 3 folder test was simplified, because creating a folder in a room is now blocked.
- Two expectations were wrong: the renumbering fallback keeps an unchanged key's change time, and the thumbnail checkbox has no accessible name.
- The join helper deadlocked by returning a promise from an async function; it now wraps it.
- `collabPages` now cancels throttled saves after each test, which fixed two tests that were flaky under coverage.

**New tests since the first coverage check:**

- 17 for the coverage gaps, including the new fake-Firestore file;
- 14 for the two manual bugs;
- 18 for the eight review bugs;
- 1 for the hash-change join path.

The current total is **330 tests across the 7 #167 test files**. [issue-167-tests.md](issue-167-tests.md) lists every one, with line links and why it's needed.

Closes #83 (Sub-issue of #14)

**Builds on #82 (merged in #180):** this branch is based on `master` after #180, so the diff contains only #83's commits.

## Why

In a busy or open room, a new collaborator is fully interactive on my screen the moment they join, so their drawings can be selected or moved by accident before I notice them. And every choice I make in the collaborator dropdown (who's hidden, who's locked, layering and its order) is lost on reload, so I have to set the room up again each session.

This PR follows the [Design comment on #83](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/83):

- **New collaborators** setting (**Visible / Locked / Hidden**, default **Locked**), applied the first time this client sees someone;
- newcomers placed **below everyone already in #82's layer order**: directly above "unknown / miscellaneous", or at the very bottom if I've moved it up (Criteria D, [amended](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/83#issuecomment-7028370098));
- the dropdown's settings are **saved locally**: the newcomer default for all rooms, and hidden, locked, the Layering switch and the order per room.

As with the rest of #14, everything stays on my device. Nothing reaches the shared scene, exports, other collaborators or undo history.

It builds on:

- **#116:** the collaborator directory ("seen before" = in the directory) and its per-room storage;
- **#81:** locking (hidden → also locked);
- **#82 (#180):** the layer order. Criteria D replaces #82's Criteria H ("newcomers go to the bottom").

## What changed

- **One pure rule.** `getNewcomerState` (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`) gives the state a first-seen collaborator starts in, built on #81's `addLockedCollaborators`. It never applies to me or to miscellaneous. #82's `getCollaboratorLayerOrder` now places newcomers directly above miscellaneous while it's the bottom row, otherwise at the very bottom; my own new client id goes on top.
- **Applied in one place.** `Collab.updateCollaborator` checks "not in the directory yet" before recording the sighting and merges the result into its existing `updateScene`. `recordSighting` is unchanged.
- **One small persistence module.** `excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorSettings.ts`: one versioned localStorage entry next to #116's directory, sharing its room pruning (20 rooms). Sets are stored as arrays; anything unreadable, unknown or from another version falls back to the defaults. Hiding my own drawings is never saved or restored.
- **Restore and save.** Restored when a room starts and right after each scene reset on join (`resetScene` resets all of appState); saved from the app's `onChange` only when a setting changed. This also stops lock and layering state leaking into the next room.
- **State and UI.** `AppState.newCollaboratorDefault` (never persisted with the scene, exported or synced), a `setNewCollaboratorDefault` action (no history), and a Visible / Locked / Hidden row in the dropdown below Layering, using the existing `RadioGroup`, on desktop and phone.
- **Snapshots:** AppState snapshots gain the new field (133 added lines, nothing else).

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- **Shared room pruning.** The settings module reuses the directory's `readStoredObject` / `withRecentRooms`, so a change to one affects the other.
- **No migration.** Saved settings from another version are ignored and replaced on the next save.
- **One browser profile = one set of saved settings.** Tabs of the same browser share a room's saved settings (last change wins) and the directory, so a collaborator first seen in one tab isn't new in another.
- **Duplicated test mocks** in `collabNewcomer.test.tsx` (socket, encryption, Firebase), as in #81/#82 (`vi.mock` is per file).
- **A typed variable in `updateCollaborator`** works around `updateScene` inferring its keys from the object literal.

**Encountered:**

- **`resetScene` resets all of appState** when joining a room; #116 republishes the directory afterwards, and this PR restores the saved settings the same way.
- **The Collab API lives in a global jotai store** that unmounting doesn't clear. Tests that re-render the app must reset it, or the new app drives the old Collab (fixed in `dba1e248` after it made reload tests flaky).
- **#116's room pruning keeps the older room** when two saves land in the same millisecond.
- **Join order after a reload** comes from the directory, which loads newest-first (accepted in #82).
- **Windows-only test setup bug:** 3 `exportToSvg` snapshots fail locally on Windows (on `master` too); CI is unaffected. On a busy machine, the first test of some files can also time out while the app loads.

## Test Evidence

| **F** Remembered after reload; default global, the rest per room | `collaboratorSettings.test.ts`: round trip of every setting, global vs per-room, Sets rebuilt, 20 rooms. `collabNewcomer.test.tsx`: real reloads (re-render on the room link) restore everything, rejoining after a reload, another room, an option chosen in the dropdown survives a reload. #81/#82 "reset on reload" tests retitled | Unit, integration (app) | **AC**; **issue discussion** (Design comment: one versioned entry, ids kept) |

Sprint 4: Feature Completion & Release[¶](#sprint-4-feature-completion-release "Permanent link")
================================================================================================

**Nov 24 – Dec 15 · All deliverables due Dec 15, 11:59 PM (course evaluation due Dec 4) · 100 points (12% of course grade)**

Sprint 4 is the last sprint of the semester. Its goal is to **finish your team feature end to end**, close your carryovers, and ship a final release of your project. The issue backlog, PR workflow, and general expectations carry forward; see [Sprint 3](../sprint3/) for anything not explicitly changed here. This page covers what is **new or different** in Sprint 4.

* * *

Sprint 4 at a glance

**Key dates:** Dec 4: course evaluation · Dec 15: everything else

**Important rules (they cost the most points):**

*   No merge without an approval on the latest commit.
*   Spec review on the issue, saying what was checked.
*   Code review on the PR, saying what was checked.
*   Every code PR links its issue.
*   Real AI logs.
*   Test Evidence table in every PR; expected values not copied from the code's output.
*   Your team introduces no new test failures; skipped tests and disabled checks need an issue.

Unfamiliar with a term?

Check the [Glossary](../glossary/) for definitions of terms used throughout this page.

* * *

### Before you begin[¶](#before-you-begin "Permanent link")

*   **Plan the rest of your team feature in the first days.** List what is left (acceptance criteria not met, sub-issues not done, bugs found in reviews), write or update the sub-issues, and get their specs reviewed. In Sprint 3, teams that split the feature late had issues that could not start until other issues were merged, and those were finished on the last day with little time for review.
*   **Order your work by dependencies.** If one issue blocks another, merge the blocking PR first and early. If a blocked issue cannot finish in time, move it out at planning time, not on the last day.
*   **Open PRs early.** Reviews need time, and the end of the semester is busy for everyone.
*   **The final presentations (Dec 1 and Dec 3) are graded separately.** See [Final Presentations](../presentations/final/). They cover your Sprint 3 work and your plan for Sprint 4.

* * *

### What is new in Sprint 4[¶](#what-is-new-in-sprint-4 "Permanent link")

*   **Lower scope minimum** (D1): about half of previous sprints.
*   **Any kind of issue counts** toward the minimum: team feature sub-issues, carryovers, bug fixes, hardening, and tech debt.
*   **Code reviews must say what was checked** (item 3 in "Things that must improve").
*   **Final report** (D6) adds a project summary, the status of your team feature, and a project retrospective.
*   **Course evaluation** (D9), due Dec 4.
*   **Removed:** mutation testing and the mid-sprint check-in.

* * *

### Things that must improve[¶](#things-that-must-improve "Permanent link")

These rules carry over from Sprint 3 and will be graded strictly. Item 3 is new.

**1\. Independent approval before merging.** A PR is merged only after a teammate approves its **latest commit**. Merging without an approval, or after pushing new commits since the approval, is not allowed. Once approved, the author may merge. Request the review on GitHub and notify your reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond (approve or request changes) within 24 hours.

**2\. Spec reviews must be visible and show what was checked.** Before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment on the issue itself. The comment states what the reviewer checked: whether each acceptance criterion is clear and testable, which cases were considered (and whether they are covered), and whether the scope fits. If the reviewer finds problems, they list them and the author updates the spec. "Looks good!" with nothing about what was checked is not acceptable.

**3\. Code reviews must show what was checked (new).** The same standard now applies to code reviews. In Sprint 3, every PR was approved before merging, but many approvals did not show any checking:

*   **Every approval should state what the reviewer checked**: for example, whether the code meets each acceptance criterion, which cases and error paths were considered, whether the tests cover the acceptance criteria and their expected values are justified, and any design or maintainability concerns.
*   **A re-approval after "changes requested" should state what was re-checked.** "Changes look good!" does not say whether the requested changes were made.
*   **AI may help draft a review, but you are responsible for it.** Edit the draft, check its claims, and remove any template text before posting.

**4\. Link PRs and issues.** Every code PR must link the issue it addresses. Use `Closes #<issue>` in the PR description and attach issues and code PRs to the `Sprint 4` milestone.

**5\. AI logs must be real logs.** A log shows your prompts and the AI's output (SpecStory format recommended; see the [AI Log Instructions](../ai-logs/)). The following are **not** logs and receive no full credit: summaries of a session, paraphrased prompts, a share link to a chat, or tool output without the prompts that produced it. File names must follow `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log from the issue or PR it documents.

**6\. The final report must render.** Check that tables and links display correctly on GitHub (no escaped `\|` or `\[`). Use the Sprint 4 sections, not a copy of a previous report.

* * *

### Deliverables[¶](#deliverables "Permanent link")

#### D1 - Sprint Backlog[¶](#d1-sprint-backlog "Permanent link")

Same process as Sprint 2 ([D1](../sprint2/#d1-sprint-backlog)), including the priority on carryovers: unfinished Sprint 3 issues go into your Sprint 4 backlog first, or you document on the issue why they are dropped.

**Scope minimums for Sprint 4** (lower than in previous sprints):

| Role | Minimum issues |

| Each CSCI 435 member | at least 1 medium issue (or equivalent story points) |
| Each CSCI 535 (grad) member | at least 1 medium issue + 1 small issue (or equivalent story points) |

**Any kind of issue counts:** sub-issues of your team feature, carryovers, bug fixes (including bugs found in reviews), hardening issues (see [Sprint 3, D1](../sprint3/#d1-sprint-backlog)), and tech debt recorded in your PRs. Finishing your team feature comes first.

**Scope must be justified.** Each issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why: which components it touches and how much change you expect. The instructor or TA may reclassify an issue whose scope is clearly overstated.

Create a `Sprint 4` milestone in GitHub and attach all selected issues to it.

**What to provide in D6 (Final report):** link to the Sprint 4 milestone and the rationale for your backlog decisions.

* * *

#### D2 - Requirements Specification[¶](#d2-requirements-specification "Permanent link")

Same as Sprint 3 ([D2](../sprint3/#d2-requirements-specification)). Specs must be written and reviewed before coding begins; see item 2 in "Things that must improve" for what counts as a review.

* * *

#### D3 - Design Decisions[¶](#d3-design-decisions "Permanent link")

Same as Sprint 2 ([D3](../sprint2/#d3-design-decisions)): each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and explains the choice.

* * *

#### D4 - Code Changes and Pull Requests[¶](#d4-code-changes-and-pull-requests "Permanent link")

Same as Sprint 3 ([D4](../sprint3/#d4-code-changes-and-pull-requests)), including the **Tech Debt** and **Test Evidence** sections in every PR description.

**Test suite.** Your team introduces no new test failures: any test your team's changes break must be fixed by the end of the sprint. Skipping a test or disabling a CI check requires a linked issue and a reason in a code comment. If your fork has no CI that runs your tests, include in the PR description the command(s) you ran and a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).

**Reviewers** post a review comment using this rubric, and the comment states what was checked (item 3 in "Things that must improve"). The **Notes** column explains each score in one or two sentences.

`## Code Review  | Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Correctness: does the change do what the issue asked? | | | | Test coverage: are tests present and meaningful? | | | | Test evidence: does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? | | | | Code quality: consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | | | | Documentation: inline comments and PR description are clear | | | | AI transparency: if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | | | | Overall: would you merge this as-is? | | |`

* * *

#### D5 - AI Logs[¶](#d5-ai-logs "Permanent link")

Same requirements as Sprint 1 ([D5](../sprint1/#d5-ai-logs)) and the [AI Log Instructions](../ai-logs/), with the enforcement described in item 5 of "Things that must improve."

**Log storage:** `ai-logs/sprint4/<your-github-username>/`

* * *

#### D6 - Final Report[¶](#d6-final-report "Permanent link")

Same format as Sprint 1 ([D6 in Sprint 1](../sprint1/#d6-sprint-report)), with these additions:

*   **Project summary** (new section). In a few sentences or bullets, describe how the system itself changed from your Sprint 0 release to your final release: what it can do now that it could not do before, what works better, and which parts of the system changed most.

*   **Team feature status** (new section). A table with one row per acceptance criterion of your team feature (from the feature issue and its sub-issues):

    | Acceptance criterion | Status | Evidence |

    | AC1: ... | Works end to end / Partial / Not done | PR, test, or manual check that shows it |

    Below the table, explain in a few sentences what is left and why. Be honest: an accurate "Partial" is better than an unsupported "Works."

*   **Project retrospective** (new section). Looking back at the whole project (Sprints 0 to 4), not only this sprint. Answer each question in a few sentences, specific to your team's experience:

    *   What worked well in your team's process (including testing and reviews), and what you would do differently if you started again.
    *   How your team's use of AI tools changed over the semester, and what the team learned about using them well.
    *   What was hardest about understanding and changing a large, existing open-source project, and how your understanding of its architecture grew.
    *   One or two concrete pieces of advice for a team starting this project next year.
*   Carryovers from Sprint 3 and what changed.

**Submit to:** `docs/sprint4/report.md` (or `.pdf`, `.docx`). If you submit Markdown, check that it renders on GitHub.

* * *

#### D7 - Final Release[¶](#d7-final-release "Permanent link")

Same as Sprint 1 ([D7 in Sprint 1](../sprint1/#d7-sprint-release)). Tag with the `-csci435-s4` suffix.

This is the final release of your project. Create it **after the last Sprint 4 merge**, so it matches the final state of your default branch. The release description summarizes the sprint's changes (features, fixes, hardening work) and states the status of your team feature, not just the tag name.

* * *

#### D8 - Reflection Survey (Individual)[¶](#d8-reflection-survey-individual "Permanent link")

Each team member must complete the Sprint 4 reflection survey individually. The link will be distributed via Blackboard and Zulip toward the end of the sprint.

**Deadline:** Dec 15, 11:59 PM.

* * *

#### D9 - Course Evaluation (Individual)[¶](#d9-course-evaluation-individual "Permanent link")

**Due: Dec 4, 11:59 PM.**

We would like to hear from you. This course is still evolving and your feedback is fundamental to improving the course. Please let us know what went well, what helped you learn, and what you would change to improve the course. Any feedback is welcome about topics, lectures, sprint structure, deliverables, AI tools, grading, etc.

Please fill out the official W&M course evaluation at [evals.wm.edu](https://evals.wm.edu/) and then submit a confirmation on the Blackboard item "Course Evaluation Confirmation." Evaluations are anonymous: the instructor sees only combined results, after final grades are submitted. We only record that you confirmed.

* * *

### Grading[¶](#grading "Permanent link")

Sprint 4 is worth **100 points** (12% of the course grade). D1, D6, and D7 are graded as a team; all other deliverables are graded individually.

| Deliverable | Points | Notes |

| D1 - Sprint Backlog | 10 | Team. Issues selected, scoped with justification, assigned, milestone created; carryover decisions documented |
| D2 - Requirements Specification | 20 | Individual. User story format, INVEST criteria, acceptance criteria quality; spec review on the issue before coding, showing what was checked |
| D3 - Design Decisions | 5 | Individual. At least one non-trivial decision per issue, with alternatives |
| D4 - Pull Requests | 27 | Individual. See detail below |
| D5 - AI Logs | 5 | Individual. Real logs, correctly named, linked from the issue or PR |
| D6 - Final Report | 15 | Team. Completeness, specificity, quality of evidence; project summary; team feature status; project retrospective |
| D7 - Final Release | 5 | Team. Tag follows convention; created after the last merge; release description summarizes changes and feature status |
| D8 - Reflection Survey | 8 | Individual. Required for completion |
| D9 - Course Evaluation | 5 | Individual. Confirmed on Blackboard by Dec 4 |
| **Total** | **100** |  |

**D4 - PR grading detail:**

The D4 score is the aggregate across all your PRs, normalized to 27 points.

| Criterion | Points per PR |

| Change correctly implements the acceptance criteria from D2 | 6 |
| Tests written or updated appropriately; Test Evidence section complete, with every AC covered and expected values justified | 6 |
| PR description explains what changed and why; Tech Debt section present; issue linked | 3 |
| CI passes (or manual verification documented); no new test failures | 3 |
| Code reviewed using the rubric; review states what was checked; PR merged only after an approval on the latest commit | 2 |
| **Total per PR** | **20** |

Reviews you write for teammates are also part of your D4 score: an approval that does not state what was checked (item 3 in "Things that must improve") lowers the review criterion for that PR.

Minimum bar

A team with no merged PRs (D4), no final report (D6), or no final release (D7) receives a **0 for Sprint 4** regardless of other deliverables.

Extra credit

*   A PR submitted to the **real upstream project** and accepted or under active review earns up to **3 bonus points** per PR, at the instructor's discretion.
*   A **bug report filed in the upstream project** that comes from your own testing work and is **confirmed by the maintainers** (by the time Sprint 4 is graded) earns up to **2 bonus points** per report, at the instructor's discretion.

* * *

### Submission checklist[¶](#submission-checklist "Permanent link")

Push the following to your team's GitHub repository **by Dec 15, 11:59 PM**:

*   Sprint 4 milestone with all selected issues attached, assigned, and scoped with justification (D1)
*   Issue bodies with user stories or bug reports, acceptance criteria, and design decisions with alternatives; spec review comments on each issue (D2, D3)
*   All PRs merged after an approval on the latest commit; each PR description links its issue and includes the Tech Debt and Test Evidence sections; code review on each PR stating what was checked (D4)
*   AI logs in `ai-logs/sprint4/<github-username>/`, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`, linked from the issue or PR (D5)
*   `docs/sprint4/report.md` (or `.pdf` or `.docx`), including the project summary, team feature status, and project retrospective (D6)
*   Final release tag pushed and GitHub release created after the last merge (D7)
*   D8 reflection survey submitted individually by **Dec 15, 11:59 PM**
*   D9 course evaluation confirmed on Blackboard by Dec 4
